title: Scratch deletes name an absolute quoted path, so the dangerous-rm prompt stops firing
why: Your question, Oct 27 00:57 CDT (cmsg_01DoF7thf3iq2Srr1UsfXgh2TP1sLyjjAdoSo7VKGT4ni8, screenshot): a degen session ran `S=<scratchpad>; cd $S; rm -rf dl/*` and Claude Code asked about a dangerous rm on the worktree's dl/*. You always accept it.
note: Cause: our command shape. Claude Code cannot follow `cd $S`, so it reads the rm as running in the worktree. That one run was safe (S was set), but the shape is a real risk: if the cd fails, rm -rf dl/* runs in the worktree. Fix: a rule that a delete names its target as an absolute or quoted-variable path (`rm -rf "$S"/dl/*`), never `cd X; rm`, and the shared shell guard refuses the `cd ...; rm <relative>` shape, printing the absolute form; red first on the screenshot's command. Also try an allow rule for the session's own scratchpad; whether a permission rule can quiet this built-in prompt is unknown, so measure it. Needs no answer. Port: yes, the guard and rule are global. Placed ahead of c116 (triage, Oct 27): it fires on you many times a day, and a prompt you always accept is spent (verification-cry-wolf-guard-is-spent).
